purpose: Readable gallery captions and story groups; proposed browsing organization, not an approved edit or exact song timeline.
timing_note: Choose shot lengths against the current song; the supplied storyboard and older plan times have not been realigned.

hon_groups.title: Pay me first
hon_groups.description: He sells the swagger: money first, help for a price.

hon_groups.title: Debt and danger
hon_groups.description: Behind the boasting, he owes money and has hunters on his trail.

hon_groups.title: The ship and the crew
hon_groups.description: His battered ship is his home; the speed, pride and friendship are real.

hon_groups.title: Turn her around
hon_groups.description: He has his money and a clear exit, yet chooses to return.

hon_groups.title: The price of love
hon_groups.description: The mercenary sacrifices his freedom for love. This is where the irony lands.

hon_groups.title: I know
hon_groups.description: Return to the refrain, let the sacrifice change its meaning, then leave room for the outro.

SB-01.lyric_connection: A flash of the grill introduces his cocky, money-first image.
SB-01.review_note: Use the close-up idea; jewelry still needs matching.

SB-02.lyric_connection: He faces the camera as if every word is a sales pitch.
SB-02.review_note: Face and small details differ from the chosen reference.

SB-03.lyric_cue: Pay me up front. You’re buying a ride.
SB-03.lyric_connection: Money changes hands before anyone boards his ship.
SB-03.review_note: Keep the transaction idea; match his face and hair.

SB-04.lyric_cue: Fuel ain’t free, and neither am I.
SB-04.lyric_connection: The empty fuel gauge makes his fee feel almost reasonable.
SB-04.review_note: Keep the fuel gag; match his face and hair.

SB-05.lyric_cue: Saving the galaxy costs extra. Nice try.
SB-05.lyric_connection: He moves through the cantina while Chewie holds down the music.
SB-05.review_note: Both the lead and DJ need appearance checks.

SB-06.lyric_connection: Chains and an arm detail underline the image he wants to project.
SB-06.review_note: The forearm lettering is an idea, not a chosen tattoo.

SB-07.lyric_connection: An elegant dinner turns into the worst invitation of his life.
SB-07.review_note: Place with the later Vader verse; the supplied early time is wrong.

SB-08.lyric_cue: Trust - trust, not safe ta play with my name
SB-08.lyric_connection: He doubles down on bravado while the debt hangs over him.
SB-08.review_note: Mouth, hair and tattoos differ from his references.

SB-09.lyric_connection: A bounty device makes the threat tangible without another speech.
SB-09.review_note: Check the hands and remove invented markings.

SB-10.lyric_connection: The debt has a face: a crime boss who expects his cut.
SB-10.review_note: Useful throne-room staging; Jabba’s final look remains open.

SB-11.lyric_connection: A rain-soaked escape turns the boasting into pressure.
SB-11.review_note: Keep the chase setting; match his face and tattoos.

SB-12.lyric_cue: not safe ta play with my name
SB-12.lyric_connection: A brief tattoo close-up adds menace to the boast.
SB-12.review_note: Confirm the blaster tattoo’s size and position.

SB-13.beat_title: The fastest junk in the galaxy
SB-13.lyric_cue: This junky ship - fastest in the galaxy!
SB-13.lyric_connection: The battered exterior gives way to an impressive burst of speed.
SB-13.review_note: Match the chosen ship silhouette before animation.

SB-14.lyric_connection: He claims the cockpit with a smirk and exaggerated captainly pride.
SB-14.review_note: Cockpit idea works; face and tattoos need matching.

SB-15.lyric_connection: A cockpit display punctuates the Kessel boast.
SB-15.review_note: Add readable display lettering during editing if needed.

SB-16.lyric_connection: A wide escape shot lets the ship prove what he has been bragging about.
SB-16.review_note: A space-action idea; the motion is still to be made.

SB-17.lyric_connection: The chest ship becomes a personal reminder of the home he defends.
SB-17.review_note: This tattoo lies sideways; the intended design points upward.

SB-18.lyric_connection: The copilot becomes the DJ, joining friendship and performance.
SB-18.review_note: The pictured copilot needs proper Chewbacca anatomy.

SB-19.lyric_cue: Got my cut. Crates in the back.
SB-19.lyric_connection: The money and cargo are secure; he has no business reason to stay.
SB-19.review_note: Useful money insert; place it by the song’s actual phrase.

SB-20.lyric_cue: I got a clean way out. Still ain’t hit the gas.
SB-20.lyric_connection: He reaches the exit and hesitates instead of taking it.
SB-20.review_note: Keep the hesitation; match the lead’s appearance.

SB-21.lyric_connection: The ship turns toward danger: the decisive choice becomes visible.
SB-21.review_note: Good direction for a turn; check the flight once animated.

SB-22.lyric_cue: Told the kid, “Good luck.” I ain’t comin’ back.
SB-22.lyric_connection: His farewell sets up the contradiction when he comes back anyway.
SB-22.review_note: Face, hair and tattoos need matching.

SB-23.lyric_connection: The copilot commits to the rescue as the old rule finally breaks.
SB-23.review_note: Match Chewbacca and check his hands on the controls.

SB-24.lyric_cue: So why’d I turn this ship around?
SB-24.lyric_connection: The rescue gives the repeated question its answer.
SB-24.review_note: Keep the rescue staging; match the lead’s appearance.

SB-25.lyric_cue: So Vader put me on ice
SB-25.lyric_connection: His heroic choice ends in a chamber where he loses his freedom.
SB-25.review_note: The lead’s face, hair and markings differ substantially.

SB-26.lyric_connection: The joke about knighthood turns bitter as the freezing begins.
SB-26.review_note: Match his appearance and lettering before animation.

SB-27.lyric_cue: Fuel ain’t free. Still paid that price.
SB-27.lyric_connection: The slab makes the cost of protecting her unmistakable.
SB-27.review_note: The frozen likeness still needs choosing.

SB-28.lyric_connection: The farewell strips away money, debt and his business pose.
SB-28.review_note: This co-star is a concept; Leia’s likeness is a separate choice.

SB-29.lyric_connection: His familiar confidence becomes an answer full of affection.
SB-29.review_note: Match the lead’s face and hair.

SB-30.lyric_connection: A thaw or reunion is an extra ending idea, not an event established by these lyrics.
SB-30.review_note: Optional only: an early reunion could weaken the sacrifice.

SB-31.lyric_connection: The stage returns for the song’s final allusions.
SB-31.review_note: The performer shown differs from the intended lead.

SB-32.lyric_connection: The DJ carries the final refrain as the performance settles.
SB-32.review_note: This image has a bear DJ; use Chewbacca for the final shot.

SB-33.lyric_cue: LISAN AL Gaib on the mic
SB-33.lyric_connection: A desert image gives the outro a possible visual allusion.
SB-33.review_note: An outro idea for this song; not automatically part of Lisan’s separate project.

SB-34.beat_title: The same face, a different meaning
SB-34.lyric_connection: Return to his opening confidence after we have seen what he sacrificed.
SB-34.review_note: The filename says lock, but the visible tattoos still differ.

SB-35.lyric_connection: A clear title card gives the acknowledgement its own moment.
SB-35.review_note: Use the intended Panhandlers lettering or logo, not this generated stand-in.

SB-36.lyric_connection: A final mouth detail or title closes the performance.
SB-36.review_note: Closing idea only; match the chosen grill and title.

lisan_groups.title: Through the mirror
lisan_groups.description: Reflection, finding a voice and the opening challenge.

lisan_groups.title: The grind and the fire
lisan_groups.description: Breaking silence, building a life, loyalty and being tested.

lisan_groups.title: Desire and creation
lisan_groups.description: What he wants, the people around him and the work they make together.

lisan_groups.title: Simplicity and hope
lisan_groups.description: Listen, cut through the noise and return to something simple.

lisan_groups.title: Into the shadow
lisan_groups.description: Archetypes, recursion and the parts of himself he must face.

lisan_groups.title: Signal in the noise
lisan_groups.description: Transformation, two worlds and a return to the microphone.
